name: WA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Emily Randall running with a large fundraising edge ($1.2M vs $28K)
No outside spending against Randall and no general-election polling
Prediction markets price Randall near certain to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Randall: a D+10 district, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage over Teresa Fox, with markets pricing her win at about 99%. With no polls or expert ratings, uncertainty stays wide, but nothing in the evidence suggests moving off a roughly 21-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much closer race or unexpected outside spending against Randall would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Emily Randall defends a western Washington seat that leans Democratic by about ten points, giving the party a solid structural edge. She has raised roughly $1.2 million and holds over $240,000 on hand, while Republican Teresa Fox has raised under $30,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Randall, and prediction markets put her chances near certain.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and market pricing. Those all point the same direction: a comfortable Democratic win, likely by around twenty points, with the usual caveat that unpolled races carry wider uncertainty.
